turns.text: Why did researchers need GPT, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?

Alec Radford and colleagues introduced the first Generative Pre-trained Transformer as a language model trained on large unlabeled text and adapted to downstream tasks. It established the decoder-only pre-training pattern that later scaled into GPT-2, GPT-3, and modern language models.

A transformer decoder predicts the next token over large text corpora, then task examples are formatted as sequences for adaptation. The same generative objective becomes a flexible interface for many language tasks.

Experts generally treat GPT as the start of the decoder-only scaling line that led to today’s large language models. Its long-term legacy is the generative pre-training recipe that turned next-token prediction into a broad interface for language tasks.
The thread continues with Vision Transformer, where researchers push the problem one step further.
